title: Partitioning & Sharding
interviewAnswer: Partitioning divides data/work across machines so systems scale. A good partition key balances load and supports common access patterns; skew creates hot partitions.
why: Partitioning & Sharding appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Partitioning divides data/work across machines so systems scale. A good partition key balances load and supports common access patterns; skew creates hot partitions. Rebalancing has operational cost. Cross-partition operations are harder. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Shard event data by hashed customer ID, but watch for a few giant tenants creating skew.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Partitioning & Sharding make?
How would you validate or debug Partitioning & Sharding in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
